You need to update all shell scripts, systemd/OpenRC unit files, deploy configs, health check scripts, proxy script rename, Python tests, and docs to reflect this rename.

The Rust code changes are already done. Do NOT touch any .rs files.

Here are the specific changes to make:

## 1. `run.sh` and `deploy/run.sh` (same change to both)
Replace `./target/release/ironclaw` with `./target/release/lunarwing`
Also replace `./target/debug/ironclaw` with `./target/debug/lunarwing` if present

## 2. `scripts/setup-instance.sh`
- `target/debug/ironclaw` → `target/debug/lunarwing`
- `target/release/ironclaw` → `target/release/lunarwing`
- `command -v ironclaw` → `command -v lunarwing`
- All help text strings: `ironclaw binary` → `lunarwing binary`, `ironclaw onboard` → `lunarwing onboard`, `ironclaw run` → `lunarwing run`
- Default libsql path: `ironclaw.db` → `lunarwing.db` (in LIBSQL_PATH default and help text)
- Error messages about the binary

## 3. `scripts/build-all.sh`
- `target/release/ironclaw` → `target/release/lunarwing` in any status messages

## 4. `scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh`
Large script. Make these changes:
- `printf '%s/target/%s/ironclaw'` → replace `ironclaw` with `lunarwing` (in lunarwing_bin function)
- `cargo "${cargo_args[@]}" --bin ironclaw` → `--bin lunarwing`
- `cargo build --bin ironclaw` → `--bin lunarwing`
- Default LIBSQL_PATH: `ironclaw.db` → `lunarwing.db`
- Database URL default: `postgres://ironclaw:ironclaw@127.0.0.1:${PG_PORT}/ironclaw` → `postgres://lunarwing:lunarwing@127.0.0.1:${PG_PORT}/lunarwing`
- `IRONCLAW_SOCKET` in env file writes → `LUNARWING_SOCKET` (but keep `IRONCLAW_SOCKET` as an alias set right after)
- `ironclaw-proxy-test.service` → `lunarwing-proxy-test.service`
- `ironclaw-proxy-mt-${tenant}.service` → `lunarwing-proxy-mt-${tenant}.service`
- `ironclaw.sock` → `lunarwing.sock` (socket filename)
- `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=info,lunarwing=info` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=info`
- Help text: `ironclaw-proxy` → `lunarwing-proxy`, `ironclaw-proxy-test.service` → `lunarwing-proxy-test.service`
- `printf '%s/tensorzero-proxy-configurations/ironclaw-proxy.py'` → `lunarwing-proxy.py`
- PostgreSQL container setup: `POSTGRES_USER=ironclaw`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=ironclaw`, `POSTGRES_DB=ironclaw` → `lunarwing`
- `pg_isready -U ironclaw` → `pg_isready -U lunarwing`
- In `_mt_seed_tenant`: `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=info,lunarwing=info,$name=debug` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=info,$name=debug`

## 5. `scripts/lunarwing-mt-admin.sh`
- `cargo build --profile $PROFILE --bin ironclaw` → `--bin lunarwing`
- `ExecStart=$repo/target/${PROFILE}/ironclaw --no-onboard run` → `lunarwing`
- `ironclaw-proxy-${name}.service` → `lunarwing-proxy-${name}.service` (everywhere this appears in service name strings)
- `/etc/init.d/ironclaw-proxy-${name}` → `/etc/init.d/lunarwing-proxy-${name}`
- `/etc/conf.d/ironclaw-proxy-${name}` → `/etc/conf.d/lunarwing-proxy-${name}`
- `rc-service "ironclaw-proxy-${name}"` → `rc-service "lunarwing-proxy-${name}"`
- Database URL: `postgres://ironclaw:ironclaw@127.0.0.1:${pg_port}/ironclaw` → `postgres://lunarwing:lunarwing@...`
- `POSTGRES_USER=ironclaw`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=ironclaw`, `POSTGRES_DB=ironclaw` → `lunarwing`
- `pg_isready -U ironclaw` → `pg_isready -U lunarwing`
- IRONCLAW_SOCKET path: `ironclaw.sock` → `lunarwing.sock`
- `ironclaw-proxy.py` → `lunarwing-proxy.py` (proxy script filename reference)
- `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=info,lunarwing=info` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=info`
- `say "building ironclaw for $name ..."` → `say "building lunarwing for $name ..."`

## 6. Systemd / OpenRC unit files
- `systemd/lunarwing.service`: `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ironclaw --no-onboard run` → `lunarwing`; `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=info,lunarwing=info` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=info`; keep `IRONCLAW_BASE_DIR` env line but ADD `LUNARWING_BASE_DIR` line above it
- `systemd/lunarwing.confd`: `lunarwing_command="/usr/local/bin/ironclaw"` → `lunarwing`; `lunarwing_rust_log="ironclaw=info,lunarwing=info"` → `lunarwing=info`
- `systemd/xmpp-bridge.service`: keep `IRONCLAW_BASE_DIR` but ADD `LUNARWING_BASE_DIR` line
- `systemd/xmpp-bridge.openrc`: ADD `export LUNARWING_BASE_DIR="${xmpp_bridge_base_dir}"` alongside the existing IRONCLAW_BASE_DIR line
- `systemd/lunarwing.openrc`: update binary path if it hardcodes `ironclaw`

## 7. Rename proxy script
Rename `tensorzero-proxy-configurations/ironclaw-proxy.py` to `tensorzero-proxy-configurations/lunarwing-proxy.py`

## 8. Deploy files
- `deploy/xmpp-bridge.service`: `PartOf=ironclaw.service` → `PartOf=lunarwing.service`; update paths referencing `ironclaw` binary
- `deploy/setup-service.sh`: `ironclaw.service` → `lunarwing.service` in systemctl commands
- `deploy/setup.sh`: file and service references: `ironclaw.service` → `lunarwing.service`; paths like `/opt/ironclaw/` → `/opt/lunarwing/` in comments and install steps
- `deploy/env.example`: DB URL default `ironclaw:CHANGE_ME@.../ironclaw` → `lunarwing:CHANGE_ME@.../lunarwing`
- `deploy/config.toml`: example command `ironclaw run` → `lunarwing run` (do NOT change `tensorzero::function_name::ironclaw`)

## 9. Health check scripts
- `ic-infrastructure-health-check/health-openrc.sh` (at /Users/cmcfee/lunarwing/ic-infrastructure-health-check/health-openrc.sh): service discovery line `/etc/init.d/ironclaw-proxy-*` → `/etc/init.d/lunarwing-proxy-*`

## 10. Python E2E tests
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py`: rename fixture `ironclaw_binary` → `lunarwing_binary` everywhere it appears; `IRONCLAW_BASE_DIR` → `LUNARWING_BASE_DIR`; `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=info` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=info`; error message strings referencing "ironclaw server" → "lunarwing server"
- `tests/e2e/pyproject.toml`: `name = "ironclaw-e2e"` → `name = "lunarwing-e2e"`

## 11. ic/CLAUDE.md
- Debugging section: `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=trace cargo run` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=trace cargo run`; `RUST_LOG=ironclaw::agent=debug cargo run` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing::agent=debug cargo run`; `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=debug,tower_http=debug` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=debug,tower_http=debug`
- `~/.ironclaw/skills/` → `~/.lunarwing/skills/` (trust model section)
- `~/.ironclaw/installed_skills/` → `~/.lunarwing/installed_skills/`
- `ironclaw tool setup` → `lunarwing tool setup`

## 12. Root-level docs (at /Users/cmcfee/lunarwing/, NOT inside ic/)
- `CLAUDE.md`: in Integration Test Harness section, binary path examples `target/release/ironclaw` → `target/release/lunarwing`; `RUST_LOG=ironclaw=` → `RUST_LOG=lunarwing=`
- `HARNESS-SINGLE-TENANT.md` and `MULTITENANCY-HARNESS.md`: any `ironclaw` binary command references → `lunarwing`

## 13. `ic/bridges/xmpp-bridge/README.md` and `ic/AGENTS.md`
- `ironclaw service install` → `lunarwing service install`
- `ironclaw service start/stop` → `lunarwing service start/stop`
- `ironclaw run` → `lunarwing run`

## 14. `ic/testing/lunarwing-xmpp/README.md`
- All command examples: `ironclaw` binary calls → `lunarwing`

Read each file before editing. Make all edits. Use `sed -i ''` for shell files.

Important notes:
- Do NOT change WebSocket subprotocol `ironclaw-agent-v1` (in codex4ironclaw/nanocode4ironclaw)
- Do NOT change `tensorzero::function_name::ironclaw`
- Do NOT change keyring service names in ic_sm/
- Keep `IRONCLAW_BASE_DIR` as a preserved legacy alias — don't remove it, just ensure `LUNARWING_BASE_DIR` is added alongside or checked first
- The proxy script at the repo root `tensorzero-proxy-configurations/ironclaw-proxy.py` should be renamed (git mv equivalent via bash mv command)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# VM bootstrap script for IronClaw on GCP Compute Engine.
3	#
4	# Run on a fresh Debian 12 VM after SSH:
5	#   sudo bash setup.sh
6	#
7	# Prerequisites:
8	#   - VM has the ironclaw-vm service account attached
9	#   - Cloud SQL Auth Proxy accessible via IAM
10	#   - Artifact Registry image pushed
11	
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	# Must run as root
15	if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
16	  echo "ERROR: This script must be run as root (sudo bash setup.sh)"
17	  exit 1
18	fi
19	
20	echo "==> Installing Docker"
21	apt-get update
22	apt-get install -y docker.io
23	systemctl enable docker
24	systemctl start docker
25	
26	echo "==> Installing Cloud SQL Auth Proxy"
27	CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_VERSION="v2.14.3"
28	CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_SHA256="75e7cc1f158ab6f97b7810e9d8419c55735cff40bc56d4f19673adfdf2406a59"
29	curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy \
30	  "https://storage.googleapis.com/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy/${CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_VERSION}/cloud-sql-proxy.linux.amd64"
31	echo "${CLOUD_SQL_PROXY_SHA256}  /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy" | sha256sum -c - || {
32	  echo "ERROR: Cloud SQL Auth Proxy checksum verification failed -- aborting"
33	  rm -f /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy
34	  exit 1
35	}
36	chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cloud-sql-proxy
37	
38	echo "==> Installing systemd services"
39	cp /tmp/deploy/cloud-sql-proxy.service /etc/systemd/system/
40	cp /tmp/deploy/ironclaw.service /etc/systemd/system/
41	systemctl daemon-reload
42	
43	echo "==> Starting Cloud SQL Auth Proxy"
44	systemctl enable cloud-sql-proxy
45	systemctl start cloud-sql-proxy
46	
47	echo "==> Configuring Docker registry auth"
48	# The VM service account provides Artifact Registry access
49	gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev --quiet
50	
51	echo "==> Creating config directory"
52	# Owned by root, readable only by root. Docker reads --env-file as root
53	# before dropping to uid 1000 (ironclaw) inside the container.
54	mkdir -p /opt/ironclaw
55	chmod 700 /opt/ironclaw
56	
57	if [ ! -f /opt/ironclaw/.env ]; then
58	  echo "WARNING: /opt/ironclaw/.env does not exist."
59	  echo "Create it with your configuration before starting IronClaw."
60	  echo "See deploy/env.example for the required variables."
61	  echo ""
62	  echo "Then run: systemctl enable ironclaw && systemctl start ironclaw"
63	else
64	  chmod 600 /opt/ironclaw/.env
65	  echo "==> Starting IronClaw"
66	  systemctl enable ironclaw
67	  systemctl start ironclaw
68	fi
69	
70	echo "==> Setup complete"
71	echo ""
72	echo "Verify with:"
73	echo "  systemctl status cloud-sql-proxy"
74	echo "  systemctl status ironclaw"
75	echo "  docker logs ironclaw"

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Health Check: OpenRC services
3	# Checks: service state, PID liveness
4	# Output: JSON to stdout
5	# Exit codes: 0=healthy, 1=degraded, 2=critical
6	
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	# Services to check (override via env: SERVICES="xmpp-bridge lunarwing")
10	# Auto-discovers multi-tenant services from /etc/init.d/ when no override is set.
11	discover_services() {
12	  local svcs=()
13	
14	  # Single-instance defaults
15	  for svc in lunarwing xmpp-bridge; do
16	    if [ -x "/etc/init.d/$svc" ]; then
17	      svcs+=("$svc")
18	    fi
19	  done
20	
21	  # Multi-tenant: lunarwing-<tenant>, xmpp-bridge-<tenant>, ironclaw-proxy-<tenant>
22	  for initscript in /etc/init.d/lunarwing-* /etc/init.d/xmpp-bridge-* /etc/init.d/ironclaw-proxy-*; do
23	    [ -x "$initscript" ] || continue
24	    local name
25	    name=$(basename "$initscript")
26	    # Skip the base single-instance names (already added above)
27	    [[ "$name" = "lunarwing" || "$name" = "xmpp-bridge" ]] && continue
28	    svcs+=("$name")
29	  done
30	
31	  if [ ${#svcs[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
32	    svcs=("lunarwing" "xmpp-bridge")
33	  fi
34	
35	  printf '%s\n' "${svcs[@]}"
36	}
37	
38	if [ -n "${SERVICES:-}" ]; then
39	  read -r -a SERVICES_ARR <<<"$SERVICES"
40	else
41	  mapfile -t SERVICES_ARR < <(discover_services)
42	fi
43	
44	issues=()
45	svc_results=()
46	overall_status="healthy"
47	overall_exit=0
48	
49	svc_json() {
50	  local name="$1" state="$2" pid="$3" status="$4"
51	  cat <<EOF
52	  {
53	    "name": "$name",
54	    "state": "$state",
55	    "pid": $pid,
56	    "status": "$status"
57	  }
58	EOF
59	}
60	
61	for svc in "${SERVICES_ARR[@]}"; do
62	  # Check if the init script exists
63	  if ! rc-service --exists "$svc" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    issues+=("service not found: $svc")
65	    svc_results+=("$(svc_json "$svc" "missing" 0 "critical")")
66	    overall_status="critical"; overall_exit=2
67	    continue
68	  fi
69	
70	  # Get service status
71	  local_status="healthy"
72	  local_exit=0
73	  state="unknown"
74	  pid=0
75	
76	  status_output=$(rc-service "$svc" status 2>&1) || true
77	  rc_exit=$?
78	
79	  # Parse state from rc-service output (typically "* status: started" or "* status: stopped")
80	  if echo "$status_output" | grep -qi "started"; then
81	    state="started"
82	  elif echo "$status_output" | grep -qi "stopped"; then
83	    state="stopped"
84	  elif echo "$status_output" | grep -qi "crashed"; then
85	    state="crashed"
86	  elif [ $rc_exit -eq 0 ]; then
87	    state="started"
88	  else
89	    state="stopped"
90	  fi
91	
92	  # Try to get PID from pidfile or supervise-daemon
93	  for pidfile in "/run/${svc}.pid" "/run/${svc}/${svc}.pid" "/var/run/${svc}.pid"; do
94	    if [ -f "$pidfile" ]; then
95	      pid=$(cat "$pidfile" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
96	      pid=${pid:-0}
97	      # Validate PID is numeric
98	      if ! [[ "$pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
99	        pid=0
100	      fi
101	      break
102	    fi
103	  done
104	
105	  if [ "$state" = "stopped" ] || [ "$state" = "crashed" ]; then
106	    local_status="critical"; local_exit=2
107	    issues+=("$svc not running: $state")
108	  elif [ "$state" = "unknown" ]; then
109	    local_status="degraded"; local_exit=1
110	    issues+=("$svc in unexpected state: $state")
111	  fi
112	
113	  if [ $local_exit -gt $overall_exit ]; then
114	    overall_exit=$local_exit
115	    overall_status=$([ $overall_exit -eq 2 ] && echo critical || echo degraded)
116	  fi
117	
118	  svc_results+=("$(svc_json "$svc" "$state" "$pid" "$local_status")")
119	done
120	
121	issues_json="[]"
122	if [ ${#issues[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
123	  issues_json=$(printf '%s\n' "${issues[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
124	fi
125	
126	svcs_json=$(printf '%s\n' "${svc_results[@]}" | jq -s .)
127	
128	cat <<EOF
129	{
130	  "component": "openrc",
131	  "status": "$overall_status",
132	  "timestamp": "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")",
133	  "metrics": {
134	    "services": $svcs_json
135	  },
136	  "issues": $issues_json
137	}
138	EOF
139	
140	exit $overall_exit
141

58	def _latest_mtime(path: Path) -> float:
59	    """Return the newest mtime under a file or directory."""
60	    if not path.exists():
61	        return 0.0
62	    if path.is_file():
63	        return path.stat().st_mtime
64	
65	    latest = path.stat().st_mtime
66	    for root, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(path):
67	        dirnames[:] = [dirname for dirname in dirnames if dirname != "target"]
68	        for name in filenames:
69	            child = Path(root) / name
70	            try:
71	                latest = max(latest, child.stat().st_mtime)
72	            except FileNotFoundError:
73	                continue
74	    return latest

106	            sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
107	            sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))

125	        else:

130	        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
131	            pass
132	        return

134	    try:

1	# IronClaw Development Guide
2	
3	**IronClaw** is a secure personal AI assistant — user-first security, self-expanding tools, defense in depth, multi-channel access with proactive background execution.
4	
5	## Build & Test
6	
7	```bash
8	cargo fmt                                                    # format
9	cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features  # lint (zero warnings)
10	cargo test                                                   # unit tests
11	cargo test --features integration                            # + PostgreSQL tests
12	RUST_LOG=ironclaw=debug cargo run                            # run with logging
13	```
14	
15	E2E tests: see `tests/e2e/CLAUDE.md`.
16	
17	## Code Style
18	
19	- Prefer `crate::` for cross-module imports; `super::` is fine in tests and intra-module refs
20	- No `pub use` re-exports unless exposing to downstream consumers
21	- No `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in production code (tests are fine)
22	- Use `thiserror` for error types in `error.rs`
23	- Map errors with context: `.map_err(|e| SomeError::Variant { reason: e.to_string() })?`
24	- Prefer strong types over strings (enums, newtypes)
25	- Keep functions focused, extract helpers when logic is reused
26	- Comments for non-obvious logic only
27	
28	## Architecture
29	
30	Prefer generic/extensible architectures over hardcoding specific integrations. Ask clarifying questions about the desired abstraction level before implementing.
31	
32	Key traits for extensibility: `Database`, `Channel`, `Tool`, `LlmProvider`, `SuccessEvaluator`, `EmbeddingProvider`, `NetworkPolicyDecider`, `Hook`, `Observer`, `Tunnel`.
33	
34	All I/O is async with tokio. Use `Arc<T>` for shared state, `RwLock` for concurrent access.
35	
36	## Extracted Crates
37	
38	Safety logic lives in `crates/ironclaw_safety/`. The `src/safety/mod.rs` shim re-exports everything for backward compatibility, but **new code should import from `ironclaw_safety` directly** (e.g. `use ironclaw_safety::SafetyLayer`). When touching a file that still uses `crate::safety::*`, migrate its imports to `ironclaw_safety::*`.

175	## Database
176	
177	Dual-backend: PostgreSQL + libSQL/Turso. **All new persistence features must support both backends.** See `src/db/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/database.md`.
178	
179	## Module Specs
180	
181	When modifying a module with a spec, read the spec first. Code follows spec; spec is the tiebreaker.
182	
183	**Module-owned initialization:** Module-specific initialization logic (database connection, transport creation, channel setup) must live in the owning module as a public factory function — not in `main.rs` or `app.rs`. These entry-point files orchestrate calls to module factories. Feature-flag branching (`#[cfg(feature = ...)]`) must be confined to the module that owns the abstraction.
184	
185	| Module | Spec |
186	|--------|------|
187	| `src/agent/` | `src/agent/CLAUDE.md` |
188	| `src/channels/web/` | `src/channels/web/CLAUDE.md` |

196	## Job State Machine
197	
198	```
199	Pending -> InProgress -> Completed -> Submitted -> Accepted
200	                     \-> Failed
201	                     \-> Stuck -> InProgress (recovery)
202	                              \-> Failed
203	```
204	
205	## Skills System
206	
207	SKILL.md files extend the agent's prompt with domain-specific instructions. See `.claude/rules/skills.md` for full details.
208	
209	- **Trust model**: Trusted (user-placed in `~/.ironclaw/skills/` or workspace `skills/`, full tool access) vs Installed (registry, read-only tools)
210	- **Selection pipeline**: gating (check bin/env/config requirements) -> scoring (keywords/patterns/tags) -> budget (fit within `SKILLS_MAX_TOKENS`) -> attenuation (trust-based tool ceiling)
211	- **Skill tools**: `skill_list`, `skill_search`, `skill_install`, `skill_remove`
212	
213	## Configuration
214	
215	See `.env.example` for all environment variables. LLM backends (`nearai`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `ollama`, `openai_compatible`, `tinfoil`, `bedrock`) documented in `src/llm/CLAUDE.md`.

Identity files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, USER.md, IDENTITY.md) injected into system prompt. Heartbeat system runs proactive periodic execution (default: 30 minutes), reading `HEARTBEAT.md` and notifying via channel if findings. See `src/workspace/README.md`.

1	# CLAUDE.md

3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## What This Repo Is
6	
7	**LunarWing** is a hard fork of IronClaw (originally by NearAI), started February 2026. The core daemon lives in `ic/`. The product name is LunarWing; `ic/` and `ironclaw` are internal/binary names from upstream.
8	
9	This is a self-hosted, privacy-first AI agent. The fork prioritizes XMPP/OMEMO, Gotify, scheduled routines, systemd deployment, and open-protocol channels. Proprietary channels (Slack, Discord, Telegram) are intentionally unsupported. Upstream compatibility is not a goal.

11	## Build & Test
12	
13	All Rust work happens inside `ic/`. Rust edition 2024, MSRV 1.92. Run from `ic/`:
14	
15	```bash
16	cargo fmt
17	cargo clippy --all --benches --tests --examples --all-features  # zero warnings required
18	cargo test                          # unit tests
19	cargo test --features integration   # + PostgreSQL tests

28	cargo check --no-default-features --features libsql  # libsql only
29	cargo check --all-features                           # both
30	```

108	
109	Before modifying complex areas, read the relevant spec. Specs are authoritative.
110	
111	| Area | Spec |
112	|------|------|
113	| Agent rules & repo contract | `AGENTS.md` |
114	| Fork goals & protected behavior | `FORK_CONTEXT.md` |
115	| Main daemon development | `ic/CLAUDE.md` |
116	| Agent loop, sessions, routines | `ic/src/agent/CLAUDE.md` |
117	| Web gateway / REST / WebSocket | `ic/src/channels/web/CLAUDE.md` |

128	## Architecture Overview
129	
130	- **Channels** normalize external input into `IncomingMessage`; `ChannelManager` merges all active streams.
131	- **Agent** owns session/turn handling, the LLM↔tool loop, approvals, and routines.
132	- **AppBuilder** is the composition root — wires DB, secrets, LLMs, tools, workspace, extensions, hooks before the agent starts.
133	- **Web gateway** is a browser-facing API/UI over the same agent/session/tool systems, not a separate product path.
134	- **XMPP bridge** runs as a separate service (systemd or OpenRC); OMEMO happens in the bridge, not the main daemon.
135	- **WASM sandbox** (wasmtime) provides isolated execution for third-party tools and channels.
136	- **Dual DB backend**: PostgreSQL (primary) + libSQL/Turso. All new persistence must support both.
137	- **TensorZero proxy** routes LLM calls via `openai_compatible` backend, enabling function-call routing and model training feedback loops. Default local endpoint: `http://192.168.1.157:3002`.
138	
139	Key extensibility traits: `Database`, `Channel`, `Tool`, `LlmProvider`, `EmbeddingProvider`, `Hook`, `Tunnel`.
140	
141	## Protected Runtime Behavior
142	
143	Do not break without explicit approval:
144	
145	- XMPP bridge operation and OMEMO encrypted chat (1:1 and group)
146	- XMPP group chat self-message suppression and live rate-limit control
147	- Gotify WASM tool usage
148	- WASM channel/tool loading
149	- Scheduled routines, manual routine runs, and stuck-run recovery
150	- Gateway status/config endpoints
151	- Systemd and OpenRC deployment units and watchdog service/timer
152	- Infrastructure health check init-system auto-detection
153	
154	## Service Operations
155	
156	- `xmpp-bridge.service` has `PartOf=ironclaw.service` — IronClaw restarts can cascade to the bridge. Do not assume the bridge caused a stop just because both restarted.
157	- Use `scripts/xmpp-rate-limit.sh` for live XMPP outbound rate-limit changes (`status`, `set <n>`, `off`, `reset`). Requires `XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN`.
158	- Use `scripts/xmpp-configure.sh` for bridge room/configuration checks.
159	- Watchdog: `scripts/lunarwing-watchdog.sh` (systemd) or `scripts/lunarwing-watchdog-openrc.sh` (OpenRC). Install via `scripts/install-lunarwing-watchdog.sh` (auto-detects init system).
160	- Prefer read-only diagnostics first (`systemctl status`, `journalctl`, gateway endpoints) before restarting services.
161	- If harness `verify` only fails the TensorZero proxy check, inspect the upstream `TENSORZERO_URL` before treating the local service install as broken.
162	- **Do not restart services or deploy binaries unless explicitly asked.**
163	
164	## Deployment & Secrets
165	
166	Secrets may live in `/home/cmc/.ironclaw/.env`, systemd service environment, DB rows, or WASM auth state. Never print secret values in logs, diffs, or responses.
167	
168	For live DB checks, use read-only SQL unless the user explicitly requests mutation. Stop the service before mutating routine state; back up the DB first.
169	
170	## Gotify Pattern
171	
172	Gotify is a WASM tool, not a channel. Routines needing Gotify notifications should call the `gotify` tool in their prompt and return the same message as backup output. See `docs/GOTIFY_ROUTINE_PROMPT.md` for the working prompt pattern.
173	
174	## XMPP / OMEMO Known Behavior
175	
176	- Bridge rejects conflicting runtime config with HTTP 409 until restarted.
177	- OMEMO encrypted group chat may take several messages after restart before decrypting reliably.
178	- Group OMEMO requires the room to be configured as encrypted in both client setup and bridge/runtime config.
179	
180	## Debugging
181	
182	```bash
183	RUST_LOG=ironclaw=trace cargo run                        # verbose all modules
184	RUST_LOG=ironclaw::agent=debug cargo run                 # agent loop only
185	RUST_LOG=ironclaw=debug,tower_http=debug cargo run       # + HTTP request logging
186	```
187	
188	## Routine System
189	
190	**Retry with backoff:** Failed routines with retryable errors (LLM timeouts, empty responses, execution timeouts) are automatically retried with exponential backoff. The per-routine `RetryPolicy` (stored in `RoutineGuardrails`) controls: `max_retries` (default 3), `initial_delay_secs` (default 60), `backoff_multiplier` (default 2.0), `max_delay_secs` (default 3600). Retries use the existing `next_fire_at` column — no new scheduler loop. After exhausting retries, the routine falls back to its normal cron schedule. Non-retryable errors (auth, config, DB) skip retry entirely. `RoutineError::is_retryable()` classifies errors.
191	
192	**Stuck-run recovery:** Lightweight routines are wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout` (default 300s, configurable via `ROUTINES_LIGHTWEIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECS`). A stuck-run sweeper runs on every cron tick to recover lightweight runs that remain in `running` state beyond the timeout. FullJob runs have separate crash recovery via `sync_dispatched_runs()`. Both mechanisms prevent a single failed run from permanently blocking its routine.
193	
194	Key config env vars: `ROUTINES_ENABLED`, `ROUTINES_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default 10), `ROUTINES_CRON_INTERVAL` (default 15s), `ROUTINES_DEFAULT_COOLDOWN` (default 300s), `ROUTINES_LIGHTWEIGHT_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 300s).
195	
196	DB migration `V18__routine_retry.sql` adds retry policy columns to the `routines` table. Both PostgreSQL and libSQL backends support the new fields.
197	
198	## Infrastructure Health Checks
199	
200	`ic-infrastructure-health-check/infrastructure-health-check.sh` orchestrates 8 parallel health checks. It auto-detects the init system and conditionally runs either `health-systemd.sh` or `health-openrc.sh` (never both). On OpenRC, `health-openrc.sh` auto-discovers multi-tenant services by scanning `/etc/init.d/` for tenant-specific init scripts.
201	
202	Override init system detection with `LUNARWING_SERVICE_MANAGER=systemd` or `LUNARWING_SERVICE_MANAGER=openrc`.
203	
204	## Multi-Tenancy
205	
206	Production multi-tenant deployments use `ic/scripts/lunarwing-mt-admin.sh`. Each tenant gets a dedicated OS user, port block (10-port range from `/etc/lunarwing/ports.json`), PostgreSQL container, TensorZero proxy, and XMPP bridge. Supports both systemd (user-level with linger) and OpenRC (system-level with supervise-daemon). See `docs/MULTITENANCY-PRODUCTION.md` for the full walkthrough.
207	
208	The test harness (`ic/scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh`) provides ephemeral multi-tenancy for development and is fully cross-platform. See `MULTITENANCY-HARNESS.md`.
209	
210	## Test Harness (`lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh`)
211	
212	`ic/scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh` is the full-stack integration test harness. It is cross-platform (Linux and macOS):
213	
214	- **Single-tenant** (`up`/`down`): always uses direct PID-file process management — works on all platforms
215	- **Multi-tenant** (`mt-up`/`mt-down`): auto-detects init system via `_mt_detect_init()` and uses the appropriate path:
216	  - **macOS**: `launchd` — generates `.plist` files in `$TEST_ROOT/launchd/`, installs to `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`
217	  - **Linux systemd**: user units in `~/.config/systemd/user/`
218	  - **Linux OpenRC**: system-level init scripts via `rc-service`
219	  - **Fallback**: direct process management
220	
221	**Key cross-platform notes:**
222	- `sed -i` portability: use `_sed_i()` helper (wraps `sed -i ''` on macOS, `sed -i` on Linux) — never call `sed -i` directly
223	- `LAUNCHD_DIR` (`$TEST_ROOT/launchd/`) mirrors `SYSTEMD_DIR` for plist artifacts
224	- `render-launchd` / `mt-render-launchd` generate validated plist files (all env vars from env files are embedded inline, since launchd has no `EnvironmentFile=` equivalent)
225	- `CLI_ENABLED=false` is always injected into launchd plists (prevents blocking stdin in daemon mode)
226	- Launchd plist labels are tenant-scoped (`com.lunarwing.test.mt-a.daemon`, `com.lunarwing.test.mt-b.daemon`) derived from the test root basename — both tenants coexist in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` without conflict. Single-tenant plists use the bare label (`com.lunarwing.test.daemon`)
227	- WASM builds on macOS require `wasm32-wasip1` and `wasm32-wasip2` targets plus `cargo-component` and `wasm-tools`. Homebrew's `rustc` lacks WASM targets — the rustup toolchain bin dir must precede `/opt/homebrew/bin` in `PATH`
228	
229	**`doctor` command** reports service status for whichever init system is present:
230	- macOS: launchd agent load status
231	- Linux systemd: `systemctl --user status`
232	- Linux OpenRC: `rc-service status`, default runlevel registration, watchdog installation (script, conf.d, cron.hourly/fcrontab)
233	- None detected: reports PID-file-only mode
234	
235	## Harness Environment Defaults
236	
237	The harness and `run.sh` intentionally set `ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=1`, `DATABASE_SSLMODE=disable`, and `PGSSLMODE=disable` for private-network Postgres/TensorZero test setups. Preserve those defaults unless explicitly changing the network or SSL assumptions.

78	| Linux (systemd) | systemd user units | `.service` in `$TEST_ROOT/systemd/` → `~/.config/systemd/user/` |
79	| Linux (OpenRC) | rc-service (direct) | direct process management fallback |
80	| Other | direct PID management | — |
81	
82	> **Note — OpenRC not yet been FULLY validated:** The OpenRC path has been implemented but has not been tested end-to-end on a real OpenRC system. (However, this task WILL be completed very soon...) `_mt_detect_init()` correctly identifies OpenRC and `doctor` reports `rc-service` status, but neither `mt-up`/`mt-down` nor single-tenant `up`/`down` have been run on Gentoo, Alpine, or any other OpenRC host. Treat the OpenRC path as best-effort until a full test is completed.
83	
84	### macOS Prerequisites
85	
86	Before running `mt-up` on macOS, ensure the WASM toolchain is set up:
87	
88	```bash
89	# 1. Both WASM targets are required (wasip1 for channels/tools, wasip2 for the daemon)
90	rustup target add wasm32-wasip1 wasm32-wasip2
91	
92	# 2. Install WASM build tools
93	cargo install wasm-tools cargo-component --locked
94	
95	# 3. Ensure rustup's rustc precedes Homebrew's in PATH.
96	#    Homebrew's rustc does NOT ship WASM targets — if it's found first, all
97	#    cargo component builds will fail with "can't find crate for `core`".
98	export PATH="$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/stable-$(rustc -vV | awk '/host/{print $2}')/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
99	which rustc   # must show ~/.rustup/toolchains/...
100	```
101	
102	Docker Desktop must be running (for PostgreSQL containers). If `docker pull` fails on first run, pull the image manually:
103	
104	```bash
105	docker pull pgvector/pgvector:pg16
106	```
107	
108	### macOS Quick Start
109	
110	```bash
111	cd ic
112	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh mt-init
113	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh build --with-wasm  # builds daemon, bridge, + all 20 WASM
114	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh mt-up              # auto-detects macOS, renders + loads plists
115	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh mt-verify
116	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh mt-down
117	```
118	
119	`mt-up` automatically renders launchd plists and calls `launchctl load` — you do not need to run `mt-render-launchd` separately. Plists are tenant-scoped (`com.lunarwing.test.mt-a.*`, `com.lunarwing.test.mt-b.*`) so both tenants coexist in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` without label conflicts. `mt-down` unloads all agents and removes them.
120	
121	### Single-tenant on macOS
122	
123	Single-tenant `up`/`down` uses direct PID management on all platforms — no launchd involvement needed. Docker (or colima) must be running for the PostgreSQL container.
124	
125	## Production Multi-Tenancy
126	
127	For production per-user multi-tenancy with OS-level isolation, see `docs/MULTITENANCY-PRODUCTION.md` and the admin script `ic/scripts/lunarwing-mt-admin.sh`. The production system provides dedicated OS users, registry-allocated port blocks, flock-serialized builds, and per-tenant PostgreSQL containers. It supports both systemd (user-level with linger) and OpenRC (system-level with supervise-daemon).
128	
129	The test harness documented here is for development/testing only. See the comparison table in `docs/MULTITENANCY-PRODUCTION.md` for the full list of differences.
130	
131	## Future Work
132	
133	- Weechat relay port integration (currently reserved, no harness plumbing yet)
134	- Per-instance worker container ports (nanocode4ironclaw, codex4ironclaw)
135	- Automatic port conflict detection in `doctor` command

1	# Agent Rules
2	
3	## Purpose and Precedence
4	
5	- `AGENTS.md` is the quick-start contract for coding agents. It is not the full architecture spec.
6	- Read the relevant subsystem spec before changing a complex area. When a repo spec exists, treat it as authoritative.
7	Start with these deeper docs as needed:
8	- `CLAUDE.md`
9	- `src/agent/CLAUDE.md`
10	- `src/channels/web/CLAUDE.md`
11	- `src/db/CLAUDE.md`
12	- `src/llm/CLAUDE.md`
13	- `src/setup/README.md`
14	- `src/tools/README.md`
15	- `src/workspace/README.md`
16	- `src/NETWORK_SECURITY.md`
17	- `tests/e2e/CLAUDE.md`
18	
19	## Architecture Mental Model
20	
21	- Channels normalize external input into `IncomingMessage`; `ChannelManager` merges all active channel streams.
22	- `Agent` owns session/thread/turn handling, submission parsing, the LLM/tool loop, approvals, routines, and background runtime behavior.
23	- `AppBuilder` is the composition root that wires database, secrets, LLMs, tools, workspace, extensions, skills, hooks, and cost controls before the agent starts.
24	- The web gateway is a browser-facing API/UI layered on top of the same agent/session/tool systems, not a separate product path.
25	
26	## Where to Work
27	
28	- Agent/runtime behavior: `src/agent/`
29	- Web gateway/API/SSE/WebSocket: `src/channels/web/`
30	- Persistence and DB abstractions: `src/db/`
31	- Setup/onboarding/configuration flow: `src/setup/`
32	- LLM providers and routing: `src/llm/`
33	- Workspace, memory, embeddings, search: `src/workspace/`
34	- Extensions, tools, channels, MCP, WASM: `src/extensions/`, `src/tools/`, `src/channels/`
35	- OpenClaw port staging work: `openclaw-ports/`. For OpenClaw port tasks, keep edits inside `openclaw-ports/` unless the user explicitly approves touching core IronClaw files.
36	
37	## Ownership and Composition Rules
38	
39	- Keep `src/main.rs` and `src/app.rs` orchestration-focused. Do not move module-owned logic into entrypoints.
40	- Module-specific initialization should live in the owning module behind a public factory/helper, not be reimplemented ad hoc.
41	- Keep feature-flag branching inside the module that owns the abstraction whenever possible.
42	- Prefer extending existing traits and registries over hardcoding one-off integration paths.
43	
44	## Repo-Wide Coding Rules
45	
46	- Avoid `.unwrap()` and `.expect()` in production; prefer proper error handling. They are fine in tests, and in production only for truly infallible invariants (e.g., literals/regexes) with a safety comment.
47	- Keep clippy clean with zero warnings.
48	- Prefer `crate::` imports for cross-module references.
49	- Use strong types and enums over stringly-typed control flow when the shape is known.
50	
51	## Database, Setup, and Config Rules
52	
53	- New persistence behavior must support both PostgreSQL and libSQL.
54	- Add new DB operations to the shared DB trait first, then implement both backends.
55	- Treat bootstrap config, DB-backed settings, and encrypted secrets as distinct layers; do not collapse them casually.
56	- If onboarding or setup behavior changes, update `src/setup/README.md` in the same branch.
57	- Do not break config precedence, bootstrap env loading, DB-backed config reload, or post-secrets LLM re-resolution.
58	
59	## Security and Runtime Invariants
60	
61	- Review any change touching listeners, routes, auth, secrets, sandboxing, approvals, or outbound HTTP with a security mindset.
62	- Do not weaken bearer-token auth, webhook auth, CORS/origin checks, body limits, rate limits, allowlists, or secret-handling guarantees.
63	- Treat Docker containers and external services as untrusted.
64	- Session/thread/turn state matters. Submission parsing happens before normal chat handling.
65	- Skills are selected deterministically. Tool approval and auth flows are special paths and must not be mixed into normal chat history carelessly.
66	- Persistent memory is the workspace system, not just transcript storage; preserve file-like semantics, chunking/search behavior, and identity/system-prompt loading.
67	
68	## Tools, Channels, and Extensions
69	
70	- Use a built-in Rust tool for core internal capabilities tightly coupled to the runtime.
71	- Use WASM tools or WASM channels for sandboxed extensions and plugin-style integrations.
72	- Use MCP for external server integrations when the capability belongs outside the main binary.
73	- Preserve extension lifecycle expectations: install, authenticate/configure, activate, remove.
74	
75	## Local XMPP and Service Operations
76	
77	- Treat systemd unit environment values as secret-bearing. Do not paste passwords, bearer tokens, or webhook secrets into user-facing output; summarize or redact them.
78	- `xmpp-bridge.service` is coupled to `lunarwing.service` with `PartOf=lunarwing.service`, so LunarWing restarts can also restart the bridge. Do not assume the bridge caused a LunarWing stop just because both units restarted together.
79	- For install-style harness tests on Linux, prefer the rendered service units over leaving `scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh up` attached to a transient shell. The durable path is `render-systemd` plus `systemctl --user` on systemd hosts; OpenRC validation should use `ironclaw service install` or the committed OpenRC templates.
80	- The harness and service path intentionally seed `ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=1`, `DATABASE_SSLMODE=disable`, and `PGSSLMODE=disable` for private-network Postgres/TensorZero test setups. Preserve those defaults unless the task explicitly changes the network or SSL assumptions.
81	- Use `scripts/xmpp-rate-limit.sh` for live XMPP outbound rate-limit changes. It requires `XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN`; `status`, `set <n>`, `off`, and `reset` are the main commands.
82	- Use `scripts/xmpp-configure.sh` for bridge room/configuration checks and configure calls when working with the existing XMPP bridge API.
83	- The local service watchdog assets are `scripts/lunarwing-watchdog.sh`, `scripts/lunarwing-watchdog-openrc.sh`, `scripts/install-lunarwing-watchdog.sh`, `systemd/lunarwing-watchdog.service`, `systemd/lunarwing-watchdog.timer`, `systemd/lunarwing-watchdog.confd`, and `systemd/lunarwing-watchdog.cron.hourly`. The installer auto-detects `systemd` vs `OpenRC`; on OpenRC it also auto-selects the scheduler. `auto` prefers an existing `cronie`/`crond`/`dcron` hourly setup and only falls back to a managed `fcron` entry when that avoids interfering.
84	- Prefer read-only diagnostics first for service issues: `systemctl status`, `systemctl show`, `journalctl`, and bridge status endpoints. Only restart services after identifying the unit state or when the user explicitly asks.
85	- If harness `verify` only fails the TensorZero proxy check, inspect the upstream `TENSORZERO_URL` before treating the local service install as broken. The local proxy can be bound and healthy while the upstream `/openai/v1/models` probe still returns `500`.
86	
87	## Docs, Parity, and Testing
88	
89	- If behavior changes, update the relevant docs/specs in the same branch.
90	- If you change implementation status for any feature tracked in `FEATURE_PARITY.md`, update that file in the same branch.
91	- Do not open a PR that changes feature behavior without checking `FEATURE_PARITY.md` for needed status updates (`❌`, `🚧`, `✅`, notes, and priorities).
92	- Add the narrowest tests that validate the change: unit tests for local logic, integration tests for runtime/DB/routing behavior, and E2E or trace coverage for gateway, approvals, extensions, or other user-visible flows.
93	
94	## Risk and Change Discipline
95	
96	- Keep changes scoped; avoid broad refactors unless the task truly requires them.
97	- Security, database schema, runtime, worker, CI, and secrets changes are high-risk. Call out rollback risks, compatibility concerns, and hidden side effects.
98	- Preserve existing defaults unless the task explicitly changes them.
99	- Avoid unrelated file churn and generated-file edits unless required.
100	- Respect a dirty worktree and never revert user changes you did not make.
101	
102	## Before Finishing
103	
104	- Confirm whether behavior changes require updates to `FEATURE_PARITY.md`, specs, API docs, or `CHANGELOG.md`.
105	- Run the most targeted tests/checks that cover the change.
106	- Re-check security-sensitive paths when touching auth, secrets, network listeners, sandboxing, or approvals.
107	- Keep the final diff scoped to the task.
108

1	# xmpp-bridge
2	
3	`xmpp-bridge` is the local sidecar used by the installable LunarWing `xmpp` WASM channel.
4	
5	It owns the real XMPP connection, OMEMO state, room membership, and outbound delivery.
6	The WASM channel talks to it over loopback HTTP.
7	
8	## Build
9	
10	```bash
11	cd bridges/xmpp-bridge
12	./build.sh
13	```
14	
15	## Run
16	
17	```bash
18	XMPP_BRIDGE_BIND=127.0.0.1:8787 \
19	XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN=change-me \
20	./target/release/xmpp-bridge
21	```
22	
23	For an isolated LunarWing/XMPP bridge test harness, including local API smoke
24	tests, live configuration wrappers, and generated user-systemd units, see
25	[`docs/LUNARWING_XMPP_TESTING.md`](../../docs/LUNARWING_XMPP_TESTING.md).
26	
27	## Services
28	
29	On Linux, `ironclaw service install` detects the host service manager:
30	
31	- systemd: installs `lunarwing.service` and, when available, a companion
32	  `xmpp-bridge.service` user unit under `~/.config/systemd/user/`
33	- OpenRC: installs `/etc/init.d/lunarwing` and `/etc/init.d/xmpp-bridge`
34	
35	`ironclaw service start` and `ironclaw service stop` manage both services
36	together when the bridge binary is available.
37	
38	If you run LunarWing as a system service instead of a user service, use the
39	production templates in:
40	
41	- `systemd/lunarwing.service`
42	- `systemd/xmpp-bridge.service`
43	
44	The main daemon unit declares `Wants=` / `After=` on `xmpp-bridge.service` so
45	the bridge starts before `ironclaw run`. The bridge unit declares
46	`PartOf=lunarwing.service` so service stops and restarts are coupled.
47	
48	## API
49	
50	- `POST /v1/configure`
51	- `GET /v1/status`
52	- `POST /v1/outbound-rate-limit`
53	- `GET /v1/messages?cursor=<n>`
54	- `POST /v1/messages/send`
55	
56	When `XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN` is set, requests must include `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
57	The server also rejects non-loopback clients.
58	
59	`GET /v1/status` includes the configured plain-room list in `configured_rooms`,
60	rooms that have produced MUC presence in `rooms_with_presence`, and the active
61	OMEMO `device_id` and `fingerprint` so you can verify or trust the LunarWing
62	device from clients like Gajim. It also reports the configured outbound XMPP
63	hourly cap (`configured_max_messages_per_hour`), the live active cap
64	(`active_max_messages_per_hour`), and how many outbound messages are still
65	counted in the current rolling hour (`outbound_messages_last_hour`).
66	
67	`POST /v1/outbound-rate-limit` lets you change the active outbound XMPP hourly
68	cap without restarting the bridge or LunarWing. Example:
69	
70	```bash
71	curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/outbound-rate-limit" \
72	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN" \
73	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
74	  -d '{"max_messages_per_hour":0}' | jq
75	```
76	
77	Set `reset_counter` to `true` if you want to clear the current rolling-hour
78	usage at the same time.

1	# LunarWing XMPP Test Environment Setup
2	
3	This is the practical setup guide for the local LunarWing and XMPP bridge test
4	environment created by `scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh`.
5	
6	The test environment is isolated from your normal `~/.ironclaw` state. By
7	default it lives at:
8	
9	```bash
10	/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test
11	```
12	
13	Use this harness when you want to test:
14	
15	- the `xmpp-bridge` sidecar HTTP API
16	- bearer-token enforcement on the bridge
17	- live XMPP bridge configuration
18	- LunarWing running against isolated state
19	- service behavior (systemd user units on Linux, launchd agents on macOS, direct PID management everywhere)
20	
21	The harness is cross-platform. Single-tenant `up`/`down` uses direct PID management on all platforms. Multi-tenant commands (`mt-*`) auto-detect the init system and use launchd on macOS, systemd on Linux, or fall back to direct management. The `doctor` command reports service status for the detected platform.
22	
23	**Platform testing status:**
24	- macOS (launchd): tested end-to-end — `mt-init`, `build --with-wasm`, `mt-up`, `mt-verify`, `mt-down` all verified
25	- Linux (systemd): implemented, not recently re-verified with current harness version
26	- Linux (OpenRC): **implemented but not FULLY tested end-to-end on a real Gentoo machine yet (will be done very soon though)** — the code path exists but has never been run on a real OpenRC system yet (Gentoo, Alpine, Artix, postmarketOS, Devuan, Hyberbola, etc.); treat as best-effort until validated...
27	
28	The `customic/` tree is not part of this setup.
29	
30	## 1. Pick a Test Root
31	
32	Use the default `/tmp` root for throwaway tests:

98	## macOS Setup
99	
100	On macOS, the WASM toolchain requires additional setup before the first `build --with-wasm` or `mt-up`:
101	
102	```bash
103	# Both WASM targets are needed (wasip1 for channels/tools, wasip2 for some components)
104	rustup target add wasm32-wasip1 wasm32-wasip2

110	**PATH ordering matters.** Homebrew installs its own `rustc` which lacks WASM targets. The rustup-managed toolchain must come first:
111	
112	```bash
113	export PATH="$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/stable-$(rustc -vV | awk '/host/{print $2}')/bin:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"

117	If `rustc` resolves to the Homebrew copy, all `cargo component build` invocations will fail with `can't find crate for 'core'`.

119	Docker Desktop must be running. If the `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` image is not cached locally, `mt-up` will pull it on first run. For multi-tenant harness usage, see `MULTITENANCY-HARNESS.md`.

121	## Fresh Recreate Recipes

187	    },

190	for path, values in updates.items():
191	    lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
192	    seen = set()
193	    out = []
194	    for line in lines:
195	        if "=" in line and not line.lstrip().startswith("#"):

197	            if key in values:

199	                seen.add(key)
200	                continue
201	        out.append(line)
202	    for key, value in values.items():
203	        if key not in seen:
204	            out.append(f"{key}={value}")
205	    path.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")

345	## Service Names
346	
347	The harness intentionally renders test services by default:
348	
349	```text
350	lunarwing-test.service
351	xmpp-bridge-test.service
352	```
353	
354	Those names avoid clobbering a real user or system service named
355	`lunarwing.service`, `ironclaw.service`, or `xmpp-bridge.service`.
356	
357	When you want the generated units to use the real LunarWing name, set both
358	service-name variables before rendering:
359	
360	```bash
361	export LUNARWING_TEST_SERVICE_NAME=lunarwing.service
362	export LUNARWING_TEST_BRIDGE_SERVICE_NAME=xmpp-bridge.service
363	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh render-systemd
364	```
365	
366	The harness uses the same names everywhere it generates dependencies:
367	
368	- the bridge unit gets `PartOf=$LUNARWING_TEST_SERVICE_NAME`
369	- the LunarWing unit gets `Wants=` and `After=` for
370	  `$LUNARWING_TEST_BRIDGE_SERVICE_NAME`
371	- `configure-bridge --restart` passes the bridge service name through
372	  `XMPP_BRIDGE_SERVICE`
373	
374	For generated user services, `configure-bridge --restart` uses
375	`systemctl --user` by default. For a machine-level service, set:
376	
377	```bash
378	export LUNARWING_TEST_SYSTEMCTL_SCOPE=system
379	```
380	
381	If you use the watchdog with a renamed service, point it at the same main unit:
382	
383	```bash
384	LUNARWING_WATCHDOG_SERVICE=lunarwing.service scripts/lunarwing-watchdog.sh
385	```

534	## 8. Generate User-Systemd Units
535	
536	This is the preferred install-style test path on systemd hosts. It keeps the
537	Postgres-backed harness alive after the invoking shell exits, which is more
538	reliable than leaving `up` running from an interactive or agent-managed shell.
539	
540	Generate test units using the current checkout, test root, and profile:
541	
542	```bash
543	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh render-systemd
544	```
545	
546	Install them for your user:
547	
548	```bash
549	mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
550	cp "${LUNARWING_TEST_ROOT:-/tmp/lunarwing-xmpp-test}/systemd/"*.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
551	systemctl --user daemon-reload
552	```
553	
554	Before using the full Postgres-backed path, make sure Docker is running because
555	the harness starts PostgreSQL in a local container.
556	
557	The generated units inherit the current harness env file, including
558	`ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=1`, `DATABASE_SSLMODE=disable`, and `PGSSLMODE=disable`.
559	
560	Starting `lunarwing-test.service` is enough; it already pulls in
561	`xmpp-bridge-test.service` and `ironclaw-proxy-test.service` through
562	`Wants=` / `After=`:
563	
564	```bash
565	systemctl --user restart lunarwing-test.service
566	systemctl --user status lunarwing-test.service
567	systemctl --user status xmpp-bridge-test.service
568	systemctl --user status ironclaw-proxy-test.service
569	```
570	
571	Use read-only diagnostics first:
572	
573	```bash
574	systemctl --user show xmpp-bridge-test.service
575	journalctl --user -u xmpp-bridge-test.service -n 100 --no-pager
576	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh bridge-status
577	```
578	
579	Stop services:
580	
581	```bash
582	systemctl --user stop lunarwing-test.service
583	systemctl --user stop xmpp-bridge-test.service
584	```
585	
586	The bridge unit has `PartOf=lunarwing-test.service`, so LunarWing service stops
587	can also stop the bridge.
588	
589	If the test stack is already running from manual `start-*` commands, stop those
590	first so the service-managed units can bind the same ports cleanly.
591	
592	The built-in Rust service installer is separate from this test renderer. Running
593	`ironclaw service install` now detects the host service manager:
594	
595	- systemd: installs the user unit as `lunarwing.service` and attempts to disable
596	  the legacy `ironclaw.service` user unit when it exists
597	- OpenRC: installs `/etc/init.d/lunarwing` and `/etc/init.d/xmpp-bridge`
598	
599	For production system services, use the committed templates instead of the
600	generated user-service units:
601	
602	```bash
603	sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 systemd/xmpp-bridge.service /etc/systemd/system/xmpp-bridge.service
604	sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 systemd/lunarwing.service /etc/systemd/system/lunarwing.service
605	sudo systemctl daemon-reload
606	sudo systemctl enable --now xmpp-bridge.service
607	sudo systemctl enable --now lunarwing.service
608	```
609	
610	Those templates expect `/etc/lunarwing/lunarwing.env` and
611	`/etc/lunarwing/xmpp-bridge.env` for production config and secrets.
612	
613	The committed `lunarwing.service` and OpenRC templates already seed
614	`ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=1` and `PGSSLMODE=disable` for private-network Postgres and
615	OpenAI-compatible lab setups. Override those in `/etc/lunarwing/lunarwing.env`
616	only when your deployment needs different SSL or network behavior.
617	
618	Install the production watchdog scheduler with:
619	
620	```bash
621	sudo scripts/install-lunarwing-watchdog.sh
622	```
623	
624	On systemd hosts, that installs `lunarwing-watchdog.timer` and
625	`lunarwing-watchdog.service`.
626	
627	On OpenRC hosts, the same installer now detects OpenRC and installs the
628	OpenRC wrapper plus either an hourly scheduler hook or a managed root
629	`fcrontab` entry.
630	
631	The default `auto` mode is conservative:
632	
633	- if `cronie`, `crond`, or `dcron` is already present, the installer keeps the
634	  cron-hourly path and does not switch you over to `fcron`
635	- if no cron-hourly daemon is present but `fcron` is available, the installer
636	  uses `fcron` instead
637	
638	Force one mode explicitly with:
639	
640	```bash
641	sudo LUNARWING_WATCHDOG_SCHEDULER=fcron scripts/install-lunarwing-watchdog.sh
642	sudo LUNARWING_WATCHDOG_SCHEDULER=hourly scripts/install-lunarwing-watchdog.sh
643	```
644	
645	`LUNARWING_WATCHDOG_CRON_DIR` still applies when you want the hourly-hook path
646	in a nonstandard directory layout.
647	
648	Migration note: the installer disables/removes old `ironclaw-watchdog` units,
649	wrappers, and hourly hooks before installing the renamed watchdog.

651	## 9. Future Targeted Checks
652	
653	Keep these as follow-up harness checks when the current setup work is stable:
654	
655	- `Live XMPP end-to-end`: use a real test JID/password plus one DM target or
656	  room to prove `/v1/configure`, polling, and outbound send work against a real
657	  XMPP service.
658	- `Secrets-only XMPP password`: remove `XMPP_PASSWORD` from `lunarwing.env`,
659	  insert it through the secret-management scripts, restart, and confirm the
660	  channel still loads from the secrets store.
661	- `Gotify real send`: add a real `gotify_app_token`, set `gotify_url`, and make
662	  the tool send one notification.
663	- `Dual-instance socket isolation`: run two harness roots at once and confirm
664	  each gets its own `run/ironclaw.sock` and `repl` attaches to the correct
665	  daemon.
666	- `Init idempotence`: run `init` twice on the same root after customizing env
667	  values and confirm the harness preserves user-edited tokens, DB mode, agent
668	  name, and XMPP fields.
669	- `DB parity`: repeat the same secret insert, restart, and verify flow once on
670	  `libsql` and once on `postgres` to catch backend-specific regressions.
671	- `Service restart behavior`: restart only `lunarwing-test.service` and confirm
672	  the DB, seeded docs, REPL socket, and XMPP migration all recover cleanly.

674	## 10. Troubleshoot
675	
676	Run:
677	
678	```bash
679	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh doctor
680	scripts/lunarwing-xmpp-test-env.sh logs 120
681	```
682	
683	Common issues:
684	
685	- `HTTP 000` from `doctor` means nothing is listening on the bridge port.
686	- `401` or `403` from `bridge-status` usually means the wrong token or env file.
687	- `gateway-status` missing `xmpp` or `weechat` usually means WASM channels were
688	  not installed yet; rerun `build --with-wasm` or `install-wasm`.
689	- `gateway-status` now reports the requested harness channels as `xmpp`,
690	  `weechat`, and `darkirc`. The Gotify tool shows up in
691	  `/api/extensions/tools` as `gotify-tool`.
692	- A system bridge may already be using `127.0.0.1:8787`; change
693	  `XMPP_BRIDGE_BIND` in the generated bridge env file.
694	- `configure-bridge` requires `jq`, `curl`, `XMPP_BRIDGE_TOKEN`, and
695	  `XMPP_PASSWORD`.
696	- If the generated systemd unit points at a missing binary, rerun `build` with
697	  the same `LUNARWING_TEST_PROFILE` used for `render-systemd`.
698	- `verify` treats the proxy as healthy when `:3002` returns any HTTP response.
699	  That confirms the local shim is running even if the upstream TensorZero
700	  service returns `404` or `500` for `GET /openai/v1/models`.

563

565	  pg_port="$(ports_get "$name" postgres)"
566	  container_name="lunarwing-pg-$name"
567	
568	  if $CONTAINER_RT inspect "$container_name" &>/dev/null; then
569	    if $CONTAINER_RT inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$container_name" 2>/dev/null | grep -q true; then
570	      say "PostgreSQL already running ($container_name, port $pg_port)"
571	      return 0
572	    fi
573	    say "starting existing PostgreSQL container $container_name"
574	    $CONTAINER_RT start "$container_name" >/dev/null
575	  else
576	    say "creating PostgreSQL container $container_name on port $pg_port"
577	    $CONTAINER_RT run -d \
578	      --name "$container_name" \
579	      -e POSTGRES_USER=ironclaw \
580	      -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=ironclaw \
581	      -e POSTGRES_DB=ironclaw \
582	      -p "127.0.0.1:${pg_port}:5432" \
583	      --restart unless-stopped \
584	      pgvector/pgvector:pg16 >/dev/null
585	  fi
586	
587	  local attempts=0
588	  while ! $CONTAINER_RT exec "$container_name" pg_isready -U ironclaw -q 2>/dev/null; do
589	    attempts=$((attempts + 1))
590	    [[ $attempts -lt 30 ]] || die "PostgreSQL for $name did not become ready"
591	    sleep 1
592	  done
593	  say "PostgreSQL ready ($container_name, port $pg_port)"
594	}
